Android requires an ongoing notification for a service that runs indefinitely.
Drag the needle to set the ceiling. The green band inside it is what the app is really using, measured — not the ceiling echoed back.

The island needs about 30–45 MB and stays there. The ceiling is a limit, not a target: raising it does not make anything faster, and the app will not grow to fill it. Earlier versions allocated real memory to meet the number on the dial, which was waste — that is gone. The reserve for Android is never touched.

The island shows at most two activities and one alert at a time whatever the ceiling says — that is a design limit, not a memory one. Raising the ceiling buys room to track more, not more on screen at once.
This ceiling is below what the island itself needs. Raise it on the gauge above.
On — a notification is cleared from the shade once the island has shown it.
Off — notifications stay in your notification shade as normal.

Two things to know before you turn this on. The brief banner at the top of the screen still appears: by the time any app is told about a notification the system has already posted it, and there is no way to suppress that. And clearing is the same as swiping it away — the notification is gone, not hidden, so if you miss the island you have missed it. Ongoing notifications are never touched.
